concepts.why: The patient presented with quadriplegia, complete sensory loss, and spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis, which are all consistent with a cervical spinal cord injury.
The patient fell out of bed, which is a traumatic event, and presented with quadriplegia and complete sensory loss, which are consistent with a traumatic spinal cord injury.
The patient presented with quadriplegia, complete sensory loss, and spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis, which are all consistent with an acute spinal cord injury.
The patient presented with spinal cord compression at C4 and C5 with anterolisthesis, which is consistent with spinal cord compression.
The patient presented with quadriplegia, complete sensory loss, and absent rectal tone, which are all consistent with cervical spondylotic myelopathy.
The patient presented with a temperature of 33.1°C, which is consistent with hypothermia.
The patient fell out of bed, which is a traumatic event, but there is no clear evidence of a traumatic brain injury.
The patient presented with urinary and stool incontinence, and absent rectal tone, which are all consistent with neurogenic bladder.
It explains the finding of abnormally hyperintense spinal cord white matter, reflecting reduced diffusion, which outlines the hypointense signal of central gray matter.
